summary:
I confirmed every verification claim in the 2a reports. I re-ran each check myself, one at a time, under capped.sh: all five typechecks exit 0, and core, webview, extension and the runner smoke files pass with exactly the counts the builders reported. The working tree is byte-identical to after_slice_2a2_built.patch and was unchanged by this review.

On the code itself, 2a1's fixed computeItems, compareTexts and closure code and the 2a2 helpers (scc, records, reveal, deps) held up. Six scratch probes found 2 major and 4 minor problems, plus 1 nit, all in 2a2:
- **Major 1 (reconcile, D2-17):** when a later step for T proposes the same premise again, it is withdrawn, and every draft of its key is dropped. The rule reads the record's stale step instead of the current draft's.
- **Major 2 (un-reject, then reconcile):** un-reject lists only the un-rejected item for reapply. The plan's inverse merge of its decision commit also brings back dependents that must stay out. The next reconcile then quietly moves such a declined item back to review, with no event, its rejected key still listed.
- **Minor 1 (Undo, own Accept):** Undo restores an own Accept whose RV-7 badges have grown since it was given.
- **Minor 2 (Undo, written premise):** undoing a Reject that took a written premise out also asks for a fresh premise write. The test does not assert the write or the restored card.
- **Minor 3 (adds no new basis):** an arrow is marked "adds no new basis" even when its source's proof uses sorry.
- **Minor 4 (contract text):** four additive fields are recorded only in §8, not in §2.2 or §2.9. If 2e leaves out the optional `ReviewState.results`, RV-11 silently never fires.

The nit is that the Accept gate and the reducer's own-Accept check run their tests in different orders, so they can give different refusal texts for the same item.

Outside the repo and scratch dir: vitest briefly wrote and deleted its bundled config in the four existing node_modules/.vite-temp folders (core, runner and webview, plus the repo root's from the extension run); all are empty again. No results or module cache was written, extension out/ and dist/ are untouched (13:47), nothing of mine is in /tmp, no processes are left, and no git, npm, npx, network or Claude was used. The probes are /tmp/claude-1000/-home-zhengyew-telelean/20626c17-0334-4498-ad86-9dc24b7010ed/scratchpad/v2a-code/probe/p1.test.ts through p6.test.ts, run with /tmp/claude-1000/-home-zhengyew-telelean/20626c17-0334-4498-ad86-9dc24b7010ed/scratchpad/v2a-code/scripts/probe.sh; logs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-zhengyew-telelean/20626c17-0334-4498-ad86-9dc24b7010ed/scratchpad/v2a-code/logs/.

findings.where: packages/core/src/review/reconcile.ts:264-280 (D2-17), with lines 216-225 and 238-249 (F5 and unchanged keys never refresh r.content)
findings.problem: D2-17 decides whether a premise draft is 'from an earlier step' by reading the record's content.premise.step. A record's content is only replaced when its content key changes, and a premise's key covers only its sentence, statement and target. So when the step that brings T's new Result version proposes the same premise again, the record still holds the earlier step's draft, and the premise is withdrawn. Line 277 then drops every draft of that key from `premises`, the later step's included. This hits a re-ask that proves T and re-proposes a premise, and a Shaky rework where 'any single item may come back unchanged' (§3.7): F5 returns P to review, then D2-17 withdraws it in the same reconcile. Claude's current proposal disappears as 'Withdrawn by Claude's step' and its draft is gone, contrary to RV-1 ('a newer proposal updates its item in place').
findings.evidence: Probe P3 (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-zhengyew-telelean/20626c17-0334-4498-ad86-9dc24b7010ed/scratchpad/v2a-code/probe/p3.test.ts). Inputs: records proof:t (fp:old) and premise:t:p (content.premise.step s1); premises [p (step s1), p (step s3), same key and text]; judgement drafts proof:t (contentKey fp:new, origin s3) and premise:t:p (same contentKey, content.premise.step s3); queueSteps ['s3']. Output: 'PREMISE status=withdrawn premises left=[] events=[{"text":"Withdrawn by Claude's step:",...}]'.
findings.fix: In section 3, take the step from the judgement's current draft: `const current = drafts.get(p.key); const pStep = current?.content.premise?.step ?? p.content.premise?.step;` and skip the premise when `pStep === step`. Filter `premises` to drop only that key's drafts from other steps: `premises.filter((x) => premiseKey(x.target, x.leanName) !== p.key || x.step === step)`. In section 1 (unchanged-key and F5-unchanged paths), set `r.content = d.content` without a rev bump, so a premise record carries its current draft (step, whyNeeded, proof, facts). Add a reconcile test: a re-ask or Submit step that proves T and re-proposes the same premise keeps it in review, with its draft in `premises`.

findings.where: packages/core/src/review/reducer.ts:455-482 (backToReview, the un-reject dependents loop) and writeOf:548-566; packages/core/src/review/reconcile.ts:226-236 (AF1 branch)
findings.problem: Per §3.6, an un-reject merges the decision commit's whole inverse patch, so 'the dependents that commit took out come back with it'. But the reducer brings back, and lists in `write.reapply`, only dependents still 'to-be-redone' with no other taker out. A dependent the user declined after it was taken out (allowed: 'to be redone -> declined'), or one whose other taker is still declined (stillOut), keeps `redo.reverted: true`. Its content is in the commit's inverse patch, though, so it returns to ws/ while the record says it is out. At the next judge, reconcile's AF1 branch treats any non-asInBase draft of a declined or reverted record as a new proposal and calls toReview, even with the same rejected content key. It adds no marker and no event. So the user's Reject (or Shaky decline) is silently reversed, and the exact rejected version sits in review with its key still in rejectedFingerprints. This breaks §3.1 'Decisions are the user's (statuses change ... by the reconcile rules, reported as events)' and §3.5's 'the same key and content key: unchanged'. In the stillOut case the restored content also cannot build without its other taker.
findings.evidence: Probe P2: Reject V (takes D1 out), Reject D1, un-reject V -> 'decl:D1: declined decline="reject" redo={"because":[V],"reverted":true}', write {revert:[], reapply:[V]}. Same with D1 declined Shaky. Reconcile of a Reject-declined, reverted record whose draft is in ws/ -> 'decl:X: in-review ... rejected=["fp:decl:X"] markers=[] events=[] problems=[]'; same for a declined record with the same key and no redo. Probe P6 (stillOut): x depends on V and W; Reject V's write reverts [V, x]; after Reject W, un-reject V gives write {reapply:[V], revert:[]} while x stays {because:[W], reverted:true}.
findings.fix: Make the un-reject's write match the inverse merge. In backToReview's un-reject, collect every item whose `redo.because` contains r.id and whose content stays out afterwards: declined with any option, still reverted (stillOut), or withdrawn. Return them so writeOf adds them to `write.revert`, which the runner applies after the merge. Record in §8 and ItemWrite that `revert` is applied after `reapply`'s inverse merge. In reconcile's AF1 branch, never silently return a Reject/plain-declined or reverted record at a judge without queueSteps. When its draft's key equals its fingerprint or is in rejectedFingerprints, keep the status and push it to `reverts` (fail closed). Report any declined-to-review change as an event. Add reducer and reconcile tests for both cases.

findings.where: packages/core/src/review/reducer.ts:913-935 (undo, the restored-Accept check; ownNeeded at line 919)
findings.problem: Undo checks restored Accepts against RV-7 only when the Accept was a group one. An own Accept recorded with belief false, restored after a judge has made the item a belief, comes back with stale badges. RV-7 says such an item returns to review. An Undo with no ws/ change makes no write, so no judge or reconcile corrects it until something else triggers one (the backstop would refuse at Apply).
findings.evidence: Probe P5: decl:X own-accepted {belief:false}, back to review (action 1); classes now BELIEF in both maps; card:z in review (or the force on); Undo -> 'status accepted, accepted {how:own, belief:false, ...}' for both forced=false and forced=true. An own Accept made now records belief:true.
findings.fix: In the restored-Accept loop, also refuse (or return the item to review with D2-23's event) when `(cls.belief && !c.before.accepted?.belief) || (cls.changesProved && !c.before.accepted?.changesProved)`, whatever `how` is, using leftOwnAccept / leftOwnAcceptProved. Add the case to the 'Redo goes through the rules' or Undo tests.

findings.problem: Undo of a Reject whose write took out a written Add premise restores 'accepted' but not the record's `card` and written `fingerprint`, though `top.takenOut` records both. So writeOf sees an accepted premise with no card and schedules a fresh premise write (`premises.write: [P]`) beside the takenOut restoration that 2e performs when inverting the action. It is harmless only if 2e's due check at step 1 runs after the restore. The returned record is inconsistent: fingerprint 'fp:draft' but accepted.fingerprint 'fp:written'. The test 'Undo of a Reject that took a written premise out restores it' asserts neither the write nor the card.
findings.evidence: Probe P1: same setup as the existing test -> UNDO OUTCOME {"write":{"action":1,"revert":[],"reapply":[],"premises":{"write":["it9989a40fd7e1e1b3"],"takeOut":[]}},"status":"accepted",...,"fp":"fp:draft"} (card undefined).
findings.fix: In `undo`, for each entry of `top.takenOut`, set the record's `card` and `fingerprint` from it before writeOf, or exclude takenOut items from `premises.write`. Extend the test to assert `write.premises.write` is [] and that the card and key are back.

findings.problem: basis(u) for 'adds no new basis' skips footprint axioms that are neither a card's .holds nor a Prop axiom of the model, so `sorryAx` disappears. An Add arrow from a source whose proof uses sorry is marked 'adds no new basis', telling the person the arrow adds nothing new although the source rests on sorry. It is only a marker, since c4 still needs the item's own Accept.
findings.evidence: Probe P4: dark.holds facts {axioms: ['Spyro.cynder_dark_past.holds','sorryAx'], usesSorry: true}, question {cynder-dark-past} -> class {..., reasons:[c4], addsNoNewBasis: true}.
findings.fix: In `basis`, return `new Set([u])` (no proof that counts) when `holds.usesSorry === true` or `holds.axioms` includes SORRY_AXIOM. Add the case to the c4 test.

findings.where: docs/slice2-plan.md §2.2 (LedgerEntry, SessionAction) and §2.9 (ReviewState); packages/core/src/review/types.ts:151, 212, 453, 458; reconcile.ts:245-248; reducer.ts:494
findings.problem: Four additive contract fields exist only in types.ts and §8: `created.draft?` (fixer 2a1), `changes[].rev`, `ReviewState.results?` and `ReviewState.labels?` (builder 2a2). The §2 code blocks that later builders 'implement as written' still show the old shapes. `results` is optional, so a 2e that builds ReviewState from §2.9 compiles without it. The reducer then records no `accepted.result`, and reconcile's RV-11 rule silently never fires: it runs only when `accepted.result !== undefined`, so an accepted Result whose verdict or Rests on changes stays accepted (fail open).
findings.evidence: grep of the plan's §2 (lines 194-1256) finds none of 'results?:', 'labels?:', 'draft?: string' or 'rev: number; before'; types.ts has all four.
findings.fix: Update the §2.2 and §2.9 code blocks with the four fields. Make `ReviewState.results` required (the runner always has the stage judgement), or have reconcile treat an accepted Result without `accepted.result` as changed (fail closed).

findings.problem: For an item that both waits for the results and has unaccepted dependencies, acceptGate (for 2c2's gates) checks 'blocked' before 'depends', while the reducer's own Accept refuses with acceptNeedsDependencies first. The view's gate text and the refusal text differ for the same item.
findings.fix: Use one order in both: missing dependencies, then waits or did-not-pass, or the reverse.
